chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Waleed ibn Sabih, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a debt of mine upon some people, so he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Say: O Allah! Grant an opportunity from Your opportunities to ease upon my debtors the repayment with it, and ease for me the collection of it through it. Indeed, You are Able over all things.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for recovering debts in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration highlights the Shia practice of seeking divine facilitation through specific moments of Allah's power (lahzat) to resolve financial obligations. The supplication emphasizes that repayment and collection are ultimately dependent on Allah's omnipotence, encouraging believers to combine practical effort with spiritual reliance (tawakkul) on the Divine. This reflects the broader jurisprudential principle that du'a serves as a means to unlock natural causes for debt recovery.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Waleed Bin Sabeeh who said,

‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> of debts of mine upon the people. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Say, 
‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Grant an opportunity from Your opportunities to ease upon my debtors they can pay off the debts with, and Ease for me the collection of these, You<sup>azwj</sup> are Able upon everything’’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad all from ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Darraj from Walid ibn Sabih who has said the following: “Once I complain to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about debts people owed to me.’
The Imam told me to say, ‘O Lord, provide an opportunity of Your opportunities in which it will be possible for my borrowers to pay and for me to receive payment. You have power over all things.’”
